hypothesis: With reuseport, 1024 client flows hash onto 16 per-thread sockets with ~±12% imbalance; the busiest socket overflows while CPUs are ~12% idle. A single shared socket lets idle threads pick up work (natural load balancing). Could win if socket-lock contention is modest; could lose badly if it isn't.

host_commands: ["ethtool -C enp8s0d1 adaptive-rx off rx-usecs 128 rx-frames 256 tx-usecs 64 tx-frames 64", "ethtool -K enp8s0d1 gro off", "sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=16777216 net.core.rmem_default=16777216", "c=0; for i in $(grep -E 'mlx4-(1[7-9]|2[0-9]|3[0-2])@' /proc/interrupts | awk -F: '{print $1}'); do echo $c > /proc/irq/$i/smp_affinity_list; c=$((c+1)); done"]

hypothesis: Per-socket load from reuseport hashing is imbalanced (~±12%), so the slowest thread's socket overflows first. With 32 worker threads/sockets (2 per CPU) the scheduler can migrate threads to even out per-CPU load. Expect +3-8% over 400k if imbalance is the limiter; a loss if context-switch overhead dominates.
